content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To make maple syrup, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Sterilize the glass storage bottles (20 minutes)
Step 2. Print and apply custom labels to the bottles (1 hour)
Step 3. Bottle the finished syrup while hot (45 minutes)
Step 4. Clean the evaporator pan for next year (2 hours)
Step 5. Transfer sap to the large boiling evaporator (30 minutes)
Step 6. Monitor the sap temperature as it rises (4 hours)
Step 7. Filter the hot syrup through a heavy felt bag (1 hour)
Step 8. Pour the finished syrup into a grading kit (10 minutes)
Step 9. Skim the "sugar sand" foam from the surface (15 minutes)
Step 10. Calibrate the syrup hydrometer (15 minutes)
Step 11. Gather firewood for the evaporator arch (3 hours)
Step 12. Purchase tapping supplies and buckets (2 hours)
Step 13. Scout the woods for healthy sugar maple trees (4 hours)
Step 14. Check the local weather forecast for freeze-thaw cycles (10 minutes)
Step 15. Measure the sugar content with a refractometer (5 minutes)
Step 16. Inspect the sap collection buckets for cracks (30 minutes)
Step 17. Final boil to reach exactly 7 degrees above boiling point (1 hour)
Step 18. Drill holes into the selected maple trees (2 hours)
Step 19. Organize the sugar shack workspace (2 hours)
Step 20. Clean the pre-filter screens (20 minutes)
Step 21. Insert spiles into the drilled holes (1 hour)
Step 22. Set up the outdoor cooking station (3 hours)
Step 23. Seal the bottles with airtight caps (30 minutes)
Step 24. Pour raw sap into a holding tank (40 minutes)
Step 25. Begin the long evaporation process (12 hours)
Step 26. Mark the identified maple trees with ribbon (2 hours)
Step 27. Hang the collection buckets on the spiles (3 hours)
Step 28. Stack the gathered firewood near the evaporator (2 hours)
Step 29. Fill the evaporator with the first batch of sap (1 hour)
Step 30. Prepare the finishing stove for the final reduction (30 minutes)
Step 31. Inventory the total volume of syrup produced (20 minutes)
Step 32. Wash the bottling funnel (5 minutes)
Step 33. Sanitize the collection buckets after use (1 hour)
Step 34. Collect sap from all the buckets in the woods (4 hours)
Step 35. Purchase a high-precision thermometer (1 hour)
Step 36. Scrub the sap storage tanks (2 hours)
Step 37. Perform a final clarity check on the liquid (15 minutes)
Step 38. Calculate the sap-to-syrup yield ratio (30 minutes)
Step 39. Wash the sap pre-filter cloth (15 minutes)
Step 40. Ignite the fire in the evaporator arch (30 minutes)
Step 41. Feed more wood into the fire to maintain a rolling boil (6 hours)
Step 42. Dry the sterilized bottles (15 minutes)
Step 43. Test the syrup density using the hydrometer (10 minutes)
Step 44. Pack the bottles into crates for storage (30 minutes)
Step 45. Level the evaporator pan to ensure even boiling (20 minutes)
Step 46. Add a drop of organic oil to reduce foaming (5 minutes)
Step 47. Dispose of the used wood ash (45 minutes)
Step 48. Order replacement felt filters (1 week)
Step 49. Tap the trees with a rubber mallet (2 hours)
Step 50. Rinse the felt filters in hot water (20 minutes)
Step 51. Set up the gravity-fed sap line (5 hours)
Step 52. Sharpen the drill bits (15 minutes)
Step 53. Clean the workspace floor (1 hour)
Step 54. Install the thermometer into the evaporator (15 minutes)
Step 55. Store the remaining firewood (1 hour)
Step 56. Sharpen the axe for splitting wood (30 minutes)
Step 57. Pour the partially reduced sap into a smaller finishing pot (30 minutes)
Step 58. Monitor the sap flow rate from the trees (2 days)
Step 59. Conduct a final taste test for quality (5 minutes)
Step 60. Clean and oil the hand tools (45 minutes)
